s1.syndrome_frame: Purpuric lesions with systemic involvement and possible paraproteinemia
salient_findings: Purpuric lesions on face, elbows, knees, and feet
Reticulated purpuric macules and patches on extensor surfaces
Skin sloughing off lesions on elbows and knees
Hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 80s
History of nonischemic cardiomyopathy and chronic kidney disease
Presented with altered mental status and unwitnessed fall
Purpuric lesions developed on nose, ear, and extensor surfaces of arms
Laboratory tests showed hypercalcemia and acute kidney injury
Rouleaux and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear
Abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses
Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis
Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels
Biopsy findings showed intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi
CT scan of pelvis revealed lytic bony lesions
Bone marrow biopsy showed hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypercalcemia, acute kidney injury, and bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction

shortlist.label: Cryoglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear, and biopsy findings showing intravascular fibrinoid material with cryoglobulins and fibrin thrombi

shortlist.label: Waldenström macroglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Monoclonal IgG-κ protein on immunofixation electrophoresis and abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses

shortlist.label: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of monoclonal protein and possible precursor to multiple myeloma or other lymphoproliferative disorders

shortlist.label: Essential mixed cryoglobulinemia
shortlist.why_kept: Purpuric lesions, elevated serum cryoglobulin levels, and absence of underlying infection or autoimmune disorder

shortlist.label: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular marrow with plasma cell proliferation and κ-light-chain restriction

shortlist.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of monoclonal protein and possible amyloid deposition in tissues

shortlist.label: Plasma cell leukemia
shortlist.why_kept: Bone marrow biopsy showing hypercellular marrow with 80% plasma cells and κ-light-chain restriction, although less likely given the absence of specific mentions of plasma cell leukemia

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with hypercalcemia, acute kidney injury, and lytic bony lesions, along with a bone marrow biopsy showing 80% plasma cells with κ-light-chain restriction, is highly suggestive of multiple myeloma. The presence of a monoclonal IgG-κ protein and abnormal paraprotein band on serum and urine protein electrophoreses further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cryoglobulinemia
rejected.why: While the patient has elevated serum cryoglobulin levels and cryoprotein precipitate on peripheral blood smear, the presence of other key findings such as hypercalcemia, lytic bony lesions, and a high percentage of plasma cells in the bone marrow biopsy are more indicative of multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Waldenström macroglobulinemia
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with IgM monoclonal protein, which is not mentioned in the patient's laboratory results.

rejected.label: Monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings are too severe to be classified as monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance, which is typically asymptomatic.

rejected.label: Essential mixed cryoglobulinemia
rejected.why: This condition is often associated with hepatitis C or other autoimmune disorders, which were not found in the patient's laboratory results.

rejected.label: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma
rejected.why: While this condition can present with monoclonal protein, the patient's bone marrow biopsy and other laboratory findings are more consistent with multiple myeloma.

rejected.label: Light-chain amyloidosis
rejected.why: The patient's laboratory results do not mention amyloid deposits, which are characteristic of this condition.

rejected.label: Plasma cell leukemia
rejected.why: This is a rare and aggressive condition that is not supported by the patient's presentation and laboratory findings.
